deep.reconstruction:
Context: thermodynamics of a non-ideal gas (an empirical 'Mariotte–Gay-Lussac plus corrections' law), probably prompted by Regnault's measurements. ϑ is a temperature-like function of pressure p and specific volume v, A is the heat equivalent of work and c_p, c_v are the specific heats.

(1) Empirical ansatz. Riemann writes
log ϑ = log p + log v + a/v + b p + c/v² + d p² + e p/v,
which is a double power-series correction to the ideal-gas law ϑ ∝ pv. He differentiates with respect to p:
∂logϑ/∂p = 1/p + b + 2d p + e/v.
He first wrote terms in a/v and c/v² and then struck them, correctly, since they do not depend on p. To first order this is ∂logϑ/∂p ≈ (1+bp)/p.

(2) Thermodynamic relation. He writes
c_p − c_v = A (∂logϑ/∂p)(∂logϑ/∂t) / (∂logϑ/∂v).
Here t is presumably the empirical temperature, and the formula is the form of the general relation c_p − c_v = A·T·(∂p/∂T)_v(∂v/∂T)_p in his variables. Rearranged:
(∂logϑ/∂v)/(∂logϑ/∂p) = A (∂logϑ/∂t)/(c_p − c_v).

(3) A model with a correction z. He puts ∂logϑ/∂p = 1/(z+p) with z = αp²/(1+β/v). The denominator he actually integrates is p + αp² + pβ/v = p(αp + 1 + β/v); this corresponds to z = αp² + βp/v.
Let k = 1 + β/v. He decomposes using the numerator trick '1 + β/v + αp − αp':
1/(p(αp+k)) = (1/k)(1/p − α/(αp+k)).
Hence, as a function of p, the solution is (1/k)·log(p/(αp+k)) plus an arbitrary function of v.
On the page he writes ϑ (or log ϑ) = log(p/(αp+1+β/v)) + 𝔙(v). The prefactor 1/k is either lost or sits in the struck-out part.
Then he differentiates in v: ∂/∂v gives a term in β/(v²(αp+k)) plus 𝔙'.
Multiplying by (z+p) = p(αp+k), as required by (2), gives
A(∂logϑ/∂t)/(c_p − c_v) = −βp/v² + 𝔙'(1+αp+β/v)p.
This would be the constraint that the specific-heat difference puts on the free function 𝔙.

(4) Right column. He begins the more general integrand dp/(p + αp² + b p/v + c'/v²), with ϑ = … + 𝔙 and its v-derivative … + 𝔙'. These are left blank or unfinished.

(5) A van der Waals-type trial. He sets
log ϑ = log(p + α/v²) + log 𝔙(v), i.e. ϑ = (p + α/v²)𝔙(v).
Then ∂logϑ/∂p = 1/(p + α/v²).
The numerator of ∂logϑ/∂v, after multiplying by (p+α/v²), is −2α/v³ + (𝔙'/𝔙)(p + α/v²).
With 𝔙 = v (my inference: 𝔙'/𝔙 = 1/v) this gives
−2α/v³ + (p+α/v²)/v = p/v − α/v³,
which is the last line on the page. So (∂logϑ/∂v)/(∂logϑ/∂p) = p/v − α/v³ for ϑ = (p + α/v²)·v.
errors: The partial-fraction integral of dp/(p(αp+k)), k = 1+β/v, is (1/k)·log(p/(αp+k)); the factor 1/k is not visible on the page. It may be in the struck-out portion, or the left side should be read as ϑ with ∂ϑ/∂p = k/(p(αp+k)).

The sign of the v-derivative looks wrong: ∂/∂v[−log(αp + 1 + β/v)] = +β/(v²(αp+1+β/v)), not −β/(v²(...)). This propagates to the −βp/v² term in the final line (it should be +βp/v² if no 1/k factor is present).
The definition z = αp²/(1+β/v) is inconsistent with the denominator actually integrated, p + αp² + pβ/v, which corresponds to z = αp² + βp/v.

The relation c_p − c_v = A ϑ_p ϑ_t / ϑ_v (in logs) is not the textbook form unless t, ϑ are interpreted appropriately (e.g. ϑ a function of the empirical temperature t). As written, its derivation is not shown and cannot be fully checked.

results.what: Empirical double-series ansatz for log ϑ(p,v) as an ideal-gas law plus corrections in p and 1/v
results.modern_name: Virial-type expansion of the equation of state (deviations from Boyle–Mariotte law)
results.usually_credited_to: Regnault's empirical fits (1840s); virial expansion formalised by Kamerlingh Onnes (1901)

results.what: Relation of c_p − c_v to partial derivatives of the temperature function
Integration of ∂logϑ/∂p = 1/(p(αp + 1 + β/v)) by partial fractions, with an arbitrary function 𝔙(v)
results.modern_name: Solving a first-order PDE in one variable with an arbitrary function of the other

results.what: Trial equation of state ϑ = (p + α/v²)·v with cohesion-type correction α/v²
results.modern_name: Van der Waals-like internal-pressure term a/v²
results.usually_credited_to: van der Waals (1873); similar corrections in Rankine and Thomson–Joule (1854)

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly routine thermodynamic manipulation of empirical gas laws. The ansatz ϑ ∝ (p + α/v²)v is formally the van der Waals attraction term (minus the covolume) and is a mildly notable unpublished detail if the page dates from the 1850s. However, it is only a trial fit form, a/v²-type corrections appear in the empirical literature of the time, and nothing is developed further.

transcription_corrections: Line 2: the struck terms are a/v² and c/v² (derivative attempts), followed by e. The page line reads '1/p + b ... e' and the next line '2dp + e/v'; the '2' is part of 2dp, not a deletion.
'∂logϑ/∂p = 1/(z+p)': the z is overwritten rather than deleted; it is the defined correction z, as confirmed by the later expression A(z+p)/(c_p − c_v)·∂logϑ/∂t.
Final block, line '[-...-] −2α/v³ + 𝔙'(p+α/v²)1/v': the struck leading fragment appears to be a fraction (𝔙'/𝔙 or similar). The factor written after 𝔙' may be 1/𝔙 rather than a separate 1/v.
